cross_product_finding: Sync Gateway's authentication layer is a pluggable front door (basic auth, deprecated social login, custom app-server delegation, OIDC) that all converge on producing one of two things: a Sync Gateway user session (Public API, channel/role-gated) or reliance on Couchbase Server RBAC credentials (Admin/Metrics API, privilege-gated - the server/ batch's model). Unlike Capella, which keys distinct privilege sets to distinct credential *types* (API key vs DB credential, etc. - see requiresCapellaRole), Sync Gateway keys distinct *authentication mechanisms* to the same single user identity/session concept; the privilege-vs-channel split happens by API surface (Public vs Admin/Metrics), not by credential type.
notable_absence: No mention of MFA, IP allowlisting, or audit logging on this page - authentication here is purely about establishing a session/identity, with all *authorization* (channel/role checks) delegated entirely to the sync function and role/user grants covered in the access-control/ pages.
